description: We are a team from Cajamarca, Peru, passionate about technology, science, and space exploration. We bring skills in programming, AI, data, design, and communication. We seek creative, curious, and collaborative people interested in games, science, space, or technology to share ideas, learn, and build an innovative project together. 🚀
summary: Mission Architect is an educational video game focused on the collaborative design and operation of space missions. It aims to help participants understand how a mission is planned beyond theory by working together to configure the spacecraft, its systems and instruments, select an orbit, and manage resources such as budget, mass, energy, and communications. During the journey to the Moon, Mars, or Jupiter, the team responds to incidents, interacts with spacecraft objects and stations to solve challenges, and observes how their decisions affect the mission. By turning these challenges into shared decisions with visible consequences, Mission Architect helps participants understand how engineering, science, and team coordination come together in a space mission. Its models and values are simplified for educational purposes.
details:
What does Mission Architect do?

Mission Architect is an educational game focused on aerospace engineering collaboration and interplanetary mission operations. It aims to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and highly complex simulators by enabling teams to design, assemble, and operate space probes through an interactive 3D environment. Participants configure spacecraft systems, evaluate engineering constraints, manage resources, and conduct scientific operations on missions to the Moon, Mars, and Jupiter. Its main innovation lies in linking engineering decisions to dynamic consequences throughout the mission, transforming space exploration into a hands-on, collaborative learning experience.

How does it work? – Main Mechanics

Mission Architect recreates the life cycle of a space mission through a three-dimensional environment. Its operation connects spacecraft configuration, engineering validation, interplanetary travel, and scientific operations, making the teams’ decisions directly affect the mission’s resources and outcomes.

  1. Spacecraft Design and Validation: Teams select a destination and a launch vehicle, then build their modular Sothara scientific probe by integrating structural, propulsion, power, thermal control, communications, and scientific instrument components.
  2. Resource and Space Environment Simulation: Throughout the mission, the simulation engine updates resources based on elapsed time, including energy consumption, battery charging, and thermal balance, which determine the spacecraft’s operating conditions during the journey.
  3. Navigation and Incident Management: The simulation allows teams to select from five orbital profiles and accelerate cruise time up to 1000x. During the journey, events such as solar storms, eclipses, and guidance anomalies occur, requiring teams to make contingency decisions before reaching their destination.
  4. Scientific Operations and Communications: Upon reaching their destination, participants can collect scientific data, store it, and transmit it to ground stations whenever communication is available. The system also simulates how distance affects signal strength and the time required for information to arrive.
  5. Cooperative Coordination and Results Review: Participants collaborate through five engineering consoles and coordinate their decisions through voting. At the end of the mission, they can reflect on their performance and understand how their individual and collective decisions influenced the mission.

What are its benefits?

It allows participants to learn how space missions are designed and developed through a 3D experience that encourages collaborative work. By interacting with spacecraft components, managing resources, and solving unexpected situations, they understand how their decisions influence the progress of a mission. Furthermore, by taking on different engineering roles, they gain insight into the various disciplines involved in a space mission while strengthening their teamwork, coordination, and decision-making skills.

What is the intended impact?

Mission Architect aims to bring space exploration and engineering closer to students and educational communities interested in science and technology.

The project seeks to provide an interactive way to explore concepts related to space missions, spark interest in space exploration and the professional fields involved, and offer opportunities to practice coordination, dialogue, and collaborative decision-making. Furthermore, since it runs in a web browser, it can be accessed without installing specialized software or requiring high-performance equipment.

What technologies did we use?

We used the following tools and technologies to develop this project:

  • TypeScript: Development of the game's logic and functionality.
  • React: Creation of the screens and user interface.
  • Babylon.js: Creation of the 3D environment and elements.
  • Supabase: Connection and synchronization between participants.
  • Zustand: Management of information and mission state.
  • Tailwind CSS: Visual design and styling of the interface.
  • Blender: 3D modeling of the spacecraft, characters, and other elements.
  • Node.js and Playwright: Testing of the project's functionality.

How is your project creative?

The creativity behind Mission Architect lies in combining 3D spacecraft construction with space mission management, aiming to represent the challenges of space exploration as realistically as possible. In this experience, every decision has consequences for the progress of the mission.

Unlike games in which components only change the spacecraft's appearance, in Mission Architect, each component serves a specific purpose and influences aspects such as weight, energy consumption, budget, and overall mission performance.

Furthermore, it is designed as a team-based experience in which participants take on different responsibilities and must coordinate to design the spacecraft, resolve incidents, and successfully carry out the mission.

What factors did your team consider?

To develop this proposal, the team primarily focused on the following aspects:

  • Using physics principles and mathematical models to represent how a space mission operates in a simplified and understandable way.
  • Ensuring that spacecraft modifications and decisions made during the journey have consequences for the progress of the mission.
  • Assigning different responsibilities to participants so that progress depends on coordination and shared decision-making.
  • Developing a 3D experience that can run in a web browser and on devices with limited resources.
  • Creating an environment inspired by space exploration and mission control centers, featuring a modular spacecraft designed specifically for the project.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Tools used: Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI), and Gemini (Google).

These tools were used to support the project development in the following areas:

  • Research and Information Gathering: Assistance with searching, reviewing, and summarizing information on space engineering methodologies and NASA scientific data.
  • Model Analysis and Adjustment: Assistance in reviewing mathematical models and adjusting values used in the simulation for educational purposes.
  • Programming and Problem-Solving: Support with code development, error detection and correction, performance improvements, and test development.
  • Writing and Translation: Assistance with drafting, reviewing, and translating project texts and documentation.
  • Visual Design and Concept Development: Exploration of visual concepts and generation of reference sketches for spacecraft interiors, interfaces, and project diagrams.
